title: Outlook: grant mailbox and folder delegate permissions from the new Outlook
summary: The briefing passes: its control paths, commands and product licensing statements are supported by Microsoft documentation. It accurately distinguishes the roadmap's unchanged development status from the sharing functionality Microsoft Support already documents, and keeps unresolved feature-specific details qualified.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity

claims.claim: Microsoft Support documents mailbox and folder sharing through Sharing and permissions in new Outlook and Outlook on the web.
claims.quote: Share and access a folder or mailbox in new Outlook; Share and access a folder or mailbox in Outlook on the web; Right-click on the folder and choose Sharing and permissions.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Documentation of these folder-sharing screens does not establish that they grant Exchange Full Access, Send as or Send on behalf.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook mailbox folder sharing permissions Full Access Send as Send on behalf private items 417063 default enable policy; opened Support sharing article, recipient permissions and calendar delegate pages. Support separates sharing without delegate access from sending on behalf.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly mapped all of this roadmap item's new screens to the permissions managed by the existing Exchange controls.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook mailbox folder sharing shared resource mailbox permissions administrator Exchange same permissions. Read Support sharing, Exchange recipient permissions, Add-MailboxFolderPermission and Outlook add-in supported-setups excerpt; none explicitly maps the complete roadmap capability.

claims.claim: Users assigned Full Access, Send as or Send on behalf permissions on another mailbox are called delegates.
claims.quote: The users that are assigned these permissions on other mailboxes or groups are called delegates.

claims.claim: An Outlook calendar delegate has the Editor calendar role.
claims.quote: An Outlook delegate has the Editor calendar role and a Delegate sharing permission flag.

claims.claim: An Outlook calendar delegate has the Delegate sharing permission flag.
claims.quote: An Outlook delegate has the Editor calendar role and a Delegate sharing permission flag.

claims.claim: Learn says to configure delegate relationships from Outlook while the calendar owner is signed in.
claims.quote: Configure delegate relationships from Outlook while the calendar owner is signed in.

claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell is appropriate for calendar folder permissions but not the preferred method for creating a complete delegate relationship.
claims.quote: Exchange Online PowerShell is appropriate for calendar folder permission administration and validation, but it isn't the preferred method for creating a complete delegate relationship.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Full Access lets a delegate open the mailbox and view, add and remove its contents.
claims.quote: Allows the delegate to open the mailbox, and view, add and remove the contents of the mailbox.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Send as makes a message appear to come directly from the mailbox without indicating the delegate sent it.
claims.quote: Allows the delegate to send messages as if they came directly from the mailbox or group. There's no indication that the message was sent by the delegate.

claims.claim: Send on behalf identifies the delegate in the From address.
claims.quote: The From address of these messages clearly shows that the message was sent by the delegate ("<Delegate> on behalf of <MailboxOrGroup>").

claims.claim: By default, Full Access delegates on a user mailbox can read its IRM-protected messages.
claims.quote: By default, for a user mailbox, Information Rights Management (IRM)-protected email messages can be read by any delegate who has Full Access permission on the mailbox.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents different prevention methods for delegates reading protected messages depending on the client.
claims.quote: User mailbox in Exchange Online | Method A or B | Method C | Method C | No prevention possible

claims.claim: Calendar delegate access does not include viewing private calendar items by default.
claims.quote: CanViewPrivateItems lets the user view private calendar items. Delegate access doesn't include this capability by default.

claims.claim: Viewing private calendar items is controlled by a separate sharing permission flag.
claims.quote: CanViewPrivateItems lets the user view private calendar items. ... The flags can be combined as Delegate,CanViewPrivateItems.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified whether this item's new screens expose the private-calendar-items flag.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook Sharing and permissions CanViewPrivateItems FullAccess SendAs mailbox folder. Read Support sharing, calendar delegate permissions and private-item client-model search excerpts; none describes this flag in the item's new sharing screens.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Sharing a subfolder requires access permissions on that folder and its parent folders.
claims.quote: The user has to grant the other person access to the specific folder that the user wants to share and also to all other parent folders in the folder hierarchy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The cited troubleshooting page requires at least Folder visible on the root Mailbox folder for the default role.
claims.quote: The root folder (the Mailbox folder) in Outlook must be assigned at least Folder visible permissions for the default role.

claims.claim: New Outlook and Outlook on the web preserve existing parent-folder permissions during sharing.
claims.quote: If these parent folders already have permissions assigned, Outlook preserves them.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: New Outlook and Outlook on the web automatically assign Folder visible where parent folders have no permissions assigned.
claims.quote: If these parent folders already have permissions assigned, Outlook preserves them. If not, it automatically assigns the minimum required permission (“Folder visible”).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Change & support
claims.claim: Insufficient folder permissions can prevent opening a shared folder with the documented logon-permissions error.
claims.quote: Unable to open default folders-you do not have permissions to logon. ... This issue occurs if the user doesn't have sufficient permissions to access the mailbox folder.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes user delegation, not an agent or automated action.
claims.quote: Delegate access for mailbox and folders can be granted from the new Outlook app. Users will be able to view the permissions granted for a mailboxes and folders.

claims.claim: Exchange supports user, shared and resource mailboxes with differences in available permission-management surfaces.
claims.quote: User mailboxes Resource mailboxes Shared mailboxes ... Send on behalf ... Note that this permission isn't available in the EAC for shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: The mailbox types covered by the complete new screen capability, particularly shared and resource mailboxes, are not specified.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook mailbox folder sharing shared resource mailbox permissions administrator Exchange same permissions. Read the record and Support sharing article; shared-mailbox/add-in search excerpts concern access to those mailboxes, not the scope of granting permissions in this roadmap item.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Using Outlook for Windows desktop, classic or new, with a Microsoft 365 organisational email address requires a plan including desktop Microsoft 365 apps.
claims.quote: To use the Outlook for Windows desktop app (either the classic or new version) with a Microsoft 365 organizational email address, you need to purchase a plan that includes the desktop versions of the Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Business Standard and Business Premium are examples of qualifying plans.
claims.quote: For example, a Business Standard or Business Premium plan provides access to a Microsoft 365 email address and the desktop versions of Outlook and other Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.claim: After adding an account with a qualifying licence, secondary accounts licensed with Business Basic or E1 can be added.
claims.quote: Once you add an account with a qualifying license to Outlook, you can add secondary accounts with licenses for products that don't include the desktop apps such as Business Basic or E1.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence or meter specific to this roadmap item is not published in the documentation checked.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook delegate sharing 417063 license pricing meter. Read licensing-options, recipient permissions and Support sharing. Support gives general qualifying Microsoft 365 subscription or Exchange Online account prerequisites; no separate entitlement or meter for this item was identified.

claims.claim: The Exchange recipient-permissions article does not list a licence prerequisite for assigning Full Access, Send as or Send on behalf.
claims.quote: You need to be assigned permissions before you can perform this procedure or procedures. To see what permissions you need, see the "Mailbox settings" entry in the Feature permissions in Exchange Online article.

claims.claim: The included licensing model refers to the published product-level Outlook licence requirement rather than a separate feature add-on.
claims.quote: For example, a Business Standard or Business Premium plan provides access to a Microsoft 365 email address and the desktop versions of Outlook and other Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for the complete roadmap capability.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook folder Sharing and permissions disable enable admin default 417063. Read record, Support sharing and Cloud Policy restrictions. They describe use and restrictions, but do not state the arrival default of this complete roadmap capability.

claims.claim: Full Access is assigned in Exchange admin center at Recipients > Mailboxes > mailbox > Mailbox Delegation > Read and manage (Full Access) > Edit > Add members.
claims.quote: In the EAC, click Recipients ... Mailboxes ... select the mailbox ... Click Mailbox Delegation ... Read and manage (Full Access) ... click Edit under the appropriate permission, and then click ... Add members.

claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell supports the printed Add-MailboxPermission call for assigning Full Access.
claims.quote: Add-MailboxPermission -Identity <MailboxIdentity> -User <DelegateIdentity> -AccessRights FullAccess -InheritanceType All [-AutoMapping $false]

claims.claim: Send as permissions are managed with Add-RecipientPermission.
claims.quote: You use the Add-RecipientPermission and Remove-RecipientPermission cmdlets to manage the Send As permission for mailboxes and groups.

claims.claim: Send on behalf permissions are managed using GrantSendOnBehalfTo on Set-Mailbox and the other corresponding recipient Set- cmdlets.
claims.quote: You use the GrantSendOnBehalfTo parameter on the various mailbox and group Set- cmdlets to manage the Send on Behalf permission for mailboxes and groups: Set-Mailbox

claims.claim: Classic Outlook exposes folder permissions at folder (right-click) > Properties > Permissions > Add > user > Add > OK > user > Permission Level.
claims.quote: Right-click the folder that you want to move, and then select Properties. ... On the Permissions tab ... Select Add. ... Select your name ... Select Add, and then select OK. ... Select your name, and then select Owner for the Permission Level.

claims.claim: Add-MailboxFolderPermission -Identity <mailbox>:\<folder> -User <user> -AccessRights <role> grants folder-level permissions using the documented parameters and identity syntax.
claims.quote: Add-MailboxFolderPermission -Identity ayla@contoso.com:\Marketing -User ed@contoso.com -AccessRights Owner ... The Identity parameter specifies the target mailbox and folder. The syntax is MailboxID:\ParentFolder[\SubFolder].

claims.claim: The cmdlet's Delegate sharing permission flag applies to calendar folders, as shown in its examples.
claims.quote: The SharingPermissionFlags parameter assigns calendar delegate permissions. This parameter only applies to calendar folders and can only be used when the AccessRights parameter value is Editor.

claims.claim: The recipient-permissions procedure requires assigned permissions and directs administrators to the Mailbox settings entry in Feature permissions in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You need to be assigned permissions before you can perform this procedure or procedures. To see what permissions you need, see the "Mailbox settings" entry in the Feature permissions in Exchange Online article.
